ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Why the P wave is inverted

A patient with a junctional rhythm has inverted P waves in leads II, III and aVF. The ventricular complexes remain narrow. Which direction of atrial depolarization best accounts for the P-wave polarity?

  1. Upward from the AV junction toward the atria
  2. Downward from the sinus node through the atria
  3. From the ventricular apex through ventricular myocardium only
  4. From the left ventricle into the aorta
  5. Random independent atrial wavelets with no organized vector
Answer and explanation

Upward from the AV junction toward the atria

Retrograde atrial activation travels superiorly, away from the positive inferior-lead electrodes.

Option explanations

Upward from the AV junction toward the atria: Retrograde atrial activation travels superiorly, away from the positive inferior-lead electrodes.

Downward from the sinus node through the atria: Normal sinus activation generally produces upright inferior P waves.

From the ventricular apex through ventricular myocardium only: A purely ventricular vector accounts for QRS activity, not an organized atrial P wave.

From the left ventricle into the aorta: Blood flow direction is not an electrical depolarization pathway.

Random independent atrial wavelets with no organized vector: Disorganized atrial activity would not produce consistent discrete retrograde P waves.
